description: Labeled questions for the query eval. Three things are scored per case: did the router pick the expected path, did the aggregation produce the right number, and did merchant resolution surface the merchants the question was actually about.
groundTruthNote: groundTruthSql is hand-written and run directly against the same database at eval time, so the expected number is derived from the data actually present rather than hardcoded. Each one must return exactly one scalar. The fuzzy cases deliberately match on merchant and raw_text rather than category: a flight, a coffee, a cab ride and a box of medicines are all narrower than any category in the closed list, which is the whole reason resolve-then-aggregate exists.

cases.question: how much did I pay for my flight booking
cases.groundTruthSql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0) FROM transactions WHERE transaction_type = 'DEBIT' AND (merchant ILIKE '%makemytrip%' OR merchant ILIKE '%make my trip%')
cases.note: The canonical case. 'Flight' is not a category - Travel also covers trains and buses - so only merchant resolution can find the rows.

cases.question: how much have I spent on coffee
cases.groundTruthSql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0) FROM transactions WHERE transaction_type = 'DEBIT' AND (merchant ILIKE '%blue tokai%' OR merchant ILIKE '%bluetokai%' OR merchant ILIKE '%starbucks%')
cases.note: Coffee is not a category either; these rows are Food & Dining alongside every restaurant and delivery order.

cases.question: how much did I spend on cab rides
cases.groundTruthSql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0) FROM transactions WHERE transaction_type = 'DEBIT' AND (merchant ILIKE '%uber%' OR merchant ILIKE '%ola%')
cases.note: Transport also holds fuel and train tickets, so the category alone overcounts.

cases.question: what have I spent on medicines
cases.groundTruthSql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0) FROM transactions WHERE transaction_type = 'DEBIT' AND (merchant ILIKE '%apollo%' OR merchant ILIKE '%pharmeasy%' OR merchant ILIKE '%pharm easy%')
cases.note: Health would also include a doctor's visit or a lab test.

cases.question: how much do my streaming subscriptions cost in total
cases.groundTruthSql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0) FROM transactions WHERE transaction_type = 'DEBIT' AND (merchant ILIKE '%netflix%' OR merchant ILIKE '%spotify%' OR merchant ILIKE '%hotstar%')
cases.note: Subscriptions is close but not the same set - it would also catch a gym membership or a news paywall.

cases.question: how much have I spent on petrol
cases.groundTruthSql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0) FROM transactions WHERE transaction_type = 'DEBIT' AND (merchant ILIKE '%indian oil%' OR merchant ILIKE '%indianoil%' OR merchant ILIKE '%bharat petroleum%' OR merchant ILIKE '%hp%')
cases.note: Fuel sits inside Transport with every cab ride.

cases.question: how much did I spend on groceries
cases.groundTruthSql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0) FROM transactions WHERE transaction_type = 'DEBIT' AND category = 'Groceries'
cases.note: The easy case: the question names a category exactly, so no resolution is needed.

cases.question: what is my total spend across all transactions
cases.groundTruthSql: SELECT COALESCE(SUM(amount), 0) FROM transactions WHERE transaction_type = 'DEBIT'
cases.note: No filtering at all. Checks that the SQL path does not invent a WHERE clause.

cases.question: how many transactions do I have in total
cases.note: A count rather than a sum, to check the aggregate itself is chosen correctly.

cases.question: what is the largest amount I have ever paid out
cases.groundTruthSql: SELECT COALESCE(MAX(amount), 0) FROM transactions WHERE transaction_type = 'DEBIT'

cases.question: show me the payment I made at the pharmacy
cases.note: Wants particular rows back, not a number. Scored on whether retrieval surfaced the pharmacy transactions.

cases.question: remind me about that large transfer I sent to someone
cases.note: Recall by meaning, with no merchant named.

cases.question: which transaction was for electronics
cases.note: 'Electronics' names no category and no merchant; only the embedding connects it to Croma.

provenance: Questions written while the router and the resolve-then-aggregate design were being built. CONTAMINATED: the flight question in this set is the reason the SQL prompt carries its 'categories are broad' paragraph and its worked ILIKE example.
